Subject: BrightDesk: Post-call qualification & next steps — model fit, evals, function-call checks

Hi Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on the model fit and structured-output/function-call surface: 

Summary of call:
- Primary use case: multi-step customer support automation (triage -> extract entities -> route). BrightDesk is most concerned about structured JSON accuracy (ticket fields), hallucination on entity extraction, and latency under 400ms p95 for short prompts.
- Data sensitivity: PII present (names/emails) — customer asked about Private deployment and KMS options; we flagged Dedicated as an option for production.

Redwood preliminary fit and recommendations:
- Recommended candidates for eval: "redwood/robin-11b-q4f16" (good balance cost/ latency) and "open/llama3-13b-quant" for higher-recall extraction tests. We also propose a smaller 4-6B model baseline to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Structured output approach: function-calling + strict JSON schema validation. We'll run schema-first tests (AJV) and schema-tolerant parsing for partial responses.

Artifacts we can provide (attached / links):
- Top-50 prompt set (attached: brightdesk_prompt_set_top50.csv) — anonymized conversation samples you shared.
- Expected JSON schema v1 (attached: brightdesk_schema_v1.json) — fields, types, enums, and allowed fallbacks.
- Benchmark report template and prior baseline (link: Redwood Drive) showing p50/p95 latency and token-cost per request.

Quality/regression concerns and mitigations:
- Regression vector: changes in stop-token handling and model updates can shift output structure (missing keys or extra nesting). Mitigation: regression tests that assert required keys + spot-check utility for semantic parity.
- Partial/malformed JSON: recommend a two-stage parser — attempt strict JSON parse, if fails run a cleaning pass (regex + bracket fixing) then re-validate. Log all repairs to audit.

Function calling / retries recommendations:
- Use explicit function signatures (name + typed args) and require idempotency tokens on critical operations.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter; max 3 retries for transient network or 5xx; do not retry on 4xx parse errors — instead surface to remediation pipeline.

Proposed immediate next steps (timeline in business days):
1) BrightDesk shares final sample of 200 prompts and labels (we asked for the top-50 now, 200 in follow-up) — you already sent top-50, thanks.
2) Redwood runs a focused fit eval on 2 models (robin-11b-q4f16, llama3-13b-q4) using your top-50 -> deliverable: structured-output accuracy, JSON-parse rate, p50/p95 latency, and cost-per-1000-requests. (ETA: 4 business days after we get the 200 sample.)
3) RFC: we will run function-call unit tests that exercise our defined function signatures and confirm mapping to internal ticket fields.
4) Joint session: review results + decide Dedicated vs Hosted pilot (30–45 min).

Attachment: brightdesk_prompt_set_top50.csv (anonymized) and brightdesk_schema_v1.json.

Questions for you before we start:
- Can you confirm SLA target for p95 latency (400ms or lower) and budget range (targeting <$0.20/request)?
- Any objections to the two-stage parsing approach for malformed JSON?

Thanks — happy to spin up the evaluation pipeline as soon as you confirm the 200-sample and SLA target.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Emma — great questions, answers inline and next steps: 

1) SLA/budget: we'll include p50/p95 latency and a cost projection at 50k/mo in the deliverable. Early expectation: robin-11b-q4f16 should be within budget for < $0.20/request in hosted mode with batching; Dedicated may lower per-request cost but requires commit. We'll include a Dedicated projection.

2) Schema-tolerant parsing: practical flow we propose:
   - Strict path: attempt function call + strict JSON parse -> pass if all required keys present.
   - Tolerant path: if strict parse fails but response contains clear key-value text, attempt cleaning / normalization (simple heuristics: bracket balancing, common quote fixes, known-key extraction) and re-validate.
   - Fallback: if tolerant path fails, return structured "partial_response" with fields we could extract and an error code; write full raw model response to audit storage. This lets BrightDesk decide whether to auto-accept partials or escalate to human-in-loop.

3) Top-50 run: yes, we can run now. We will keep PII inside Redwood test infra under the scope of the eval and redact logs in the shared report. Please confirm if BrightDesk wants unredacted outputs to be sent directly to your S3 (we can push) or redacted in our Drive report.

4) Function-calling and long arrays: function-calling works with long arrays, but it increases token usage and latency. For very long arrays (ticket history > 10 items) we recommend either:
   - Pre-truncate or summarize history before calling the model, or
   - Use a two-step flow: extraction on recent items + background summarization of older history.

Attached to this reply: brightdesk_schema_v1.json (updated with explicit "required" keys and example payloads).

Internal ask (Monica / Ben): please run a quick smoke on the top-50 against robin-11b-q4f16 and llama3-13b-q4 on our eval infra (use the "structured-output" job template under /teams/brightdesk). Deliverable: raw outputs, parse success rate, examples of repaired JSON, and p50/p95 latency. Can you have an initial pass by 2026-12-24 EOD?

Proposed joint review: 2026-12-28 10:00 AM PT for results + pilot decision. If that works, Emma/Sam, please share calendar invite.

Thanks — Rafael

Rafael Mendes
